newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge by daily limits.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge by daily limits.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher on Monday, with all months except for the spot September contract ending up by their daily 400 yen limits, traders said.
The higher Chicago market on Friday, along with strong soybean futures prices at home, triggered active buying interest from private investors, they said.
The benchmark July 1998 contract was up 400 yen at 15,290 yen per tonne. Activity was buoyant with estimated volume at 136,3762 lots.
"A rise in the CBOT project A trading amid concern over hot and dry weather conditions in the U.S., added bullishness to the market," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.72 per bushel at 0818 GMT, against $2.68-1/2 at Friday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $7.73 per bushel at 0819 GMT, against $7.62 at Friday's close.
